issues.legal_issue: Construction on forest land for a purpose beyond the specifically approved use is unlawful, and an unauthorized structure may be ordered demolished.
material_facts: The forest land had been approved for construction of a parking place and a bus stand, not a hotel, restaurant, or commercial complex.
A hotel-cum-restaurant structure was constructed on the forest land without prior approval for that use.
A later request to change the approved use of the land was refused.
The construction proceeded despite planning authorities’ efforts to halt it and did not conform to the plans proposed for the project.
issues.conclusion: The construction of the hotel-cum-restaurant structure was illegal, and the order requiring its demolition was upheld. The Court directed that demolition be commenced and completed, with public authorities to carry it out and recover the costs if the responsible contractor defaulted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2 of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires prior Central Government approval for using forest land for a non-forest purpose and requires strict, punctilious compliance; approval for one specified use does not authorize a different use. The Court applied the environmental rule of law and relied on Hanuman Laxman Aroskar v Union of India, Goel Ganga Developers India Pvt. Ltd. v Union of India, M.C. Mehta v Union of India, and Hospitality Association of Mudumalai v In Defence of Environment and Animals in emphasizing compliance with environmental law and effective remedies for violations.

rule.if: appeal_from_environmental_tribunal and forest_land_approved_only_for_a_specific_use and structure_built_for_a_different_use and no_prior_approval_for_different_use

predicates.appeal_from_environmental_tribunal: A party brought an appeal from an environmental tribunal’s decision concerning construction on land.
predicates.forest_land_approved_only_for_a_specific: The competent authority approved forest land for a specified use and no broader use.
predicates.structure_built_for_a_different_use: A project proponent constructed a structure for a purpose different from the approved use.
predicates.no_prior_approval_for_different_use: The project proponent did not obtain prior approval for the different use of the forest land.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns construction on forest land approved only for a specific use, and a structure was built for another use without prior approval, the rule requires demolition of the unauthorized structure.

issues.legal_issue: The environmental tribunal may adjudicate a planning-law violation when the dispute raises a substantial environmental question arising from implementation of an enactment within its jurisdiction.
material_facts: The project was constructed without the planning department’s approval of its plans, and the planning department had called for construction to stop.
The tribunal considered the planning-law violation alongside the project’s use of forest land without the required approval.
The tribunal’s decision also rested on a violation of the forest-conservation requirements, an enactment within the tribunal’s jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal could consider the planning-law violation because it concerned an environmental obligation; in any event, the question was academic because the tribunal’s decision was independently grounded in the forest-law violation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14 and 2(1)(m) of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 permit the tribunal to decide civil cases involving a substantial question relating to the environment arising from implementation of an enactment in Schedule I. A specific environmental obligation may give rise to such a question even if the law creating the obligation is not itself listed in Schedule I, provided the question arises from implementation of a listed enactment. The Court relied on State of M.P. v Centre for Environment Protection Research & Development.

predicates.appeal_from_environmental_tribunal: A party appealed a decision made by an environmental tribunal.
predicates.substantial_environmental_question: The dispute raised a substantial question concerning an environmental right or obligation affecting the environment or a community.
predicates.question_arises_from_covered_environment: The environmental question arose from implementation of an enactment that the tribunal is empowered to apply.

issues.definition: If an appeal from an environmental tribunal involves a substantial environmental question arising from implementation of an enactment within the tribunal’s jurisdiction, the tribunal may decide the related environmental planning violation.
